unresolvedReferences.description: The phrase 九節度嬰、籠官馬定德 is ambiguous: the literal English reads 嬰 (Ying) as the name of the Tibetan chieftain-overseer, while the idiomatic English omits it; p025 is recorded with uncertain certainty.
乃反昪疾趨隴州: 昪 appears to be a textual corruption (context suggests feigning illness, as in s0007); translations assume 'feigning illness'.
The source dates the presentation of the captive Lun Mangre to 是歲十月 (Zhenyuan 17); the subject who sent the envoy is unstated and inferred as Wei Gao.
The chapter does not state whether Emperor Xianzong is the crown prince of s0090–s0091; they are kept as separate local records.
Xingshi is Wei Gao's nephew (侄), but which sibling of Wei Gao was his parent is not stated, so no intermediary parent record is created.
皇祖玄元 is taken as Laozi (the deified Xuanyuan Emperor, claimed ancestor of the Tang house); the chapter does not name him.
上 ('the emperor') in the Yuanhe 1 narrative is taken as Emperor Xianzong, named in the preceding read-only context (s0107).
The subject of 尋稱偽號，改元 is read as Li Xilie (sender of the amnesties to Chen Shaoyou and Jianfeng); the current idiomatic English makes Chen Shaoyou the pretender.
嗣曹王臯 names the Heir Prince of Cao only by his given name 臯; the surname Li comes from the English translation. He is distinct from Wei Gao (韋臯).
衛、霍 are read as the Western Han generals Wei Qing and Huo Qubing (as in the translation); their Western intervals come from outside research, not from this chapter.
